'''Tomato and egg soup''' ({{zh|s=番茄蛋汤|p=Fānqié dàn tāng
}} or {{zh|s=番茄蛋花汤|p=Fānqié dàn huā tāng}}) is a dish from [[China]] consisting mainly of [[tomato]] and [[egg (food)|egg]].<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=Bh1BAAAAYAAJ ''Recipes of all nations''], [[Countess Morphy]], p.258</ref><ref>''Food of Asia'' Lynn Lewis, Murdoch Books, p.100</ref> It is a relatively easy [[soup]] to make, and as such is one of the most popular soups in households.<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=-9XWQrpbLAgC ''Food of China''], Nina Simonds, p.60</ref>

Normally, the soup is made from coarsely chopped tomatoes, and green onions chopped to pieces of about of 0.5 cm. Half a litre of water is used in this soup, and a small amount of oil. Eggs are added toward the end of this dish, and stirred in for only about 3 minutes. It is normally covered for 2 minutes, and then served when the egg has set.

This soup is also sometimes made with the tomato skin removed, and is sometimes cooked for a longer time.
